_comments: Sample configuration for GENERIC mode -- connecting to any JDBC-compliant data source
not otherwise recognized by orm_skyway (requires JDX 5.22+).
In GENERIC mode, JDX passes every non-JDX-internal property straight through to your
JDBC driver, with no whitelist filtering. JDX's own internal keys (JDX_DBTYPE,
DEBUG_LEVEL, JDX_ORMFile, etc.) are automatically excluded from what gets forwarded.
Put any driver-specific connection properties your database needs directly in jdbc_url,
in either format -- both work, use whichever your specific driver expects:
Semicolon-separated: jdbc:db://host/db;key=val;key2=val2
Query string:        jdbc:db://host/db?key=val&key2=val2
The example jdbc_url below shows apiKey and timeout as placeholder driver-specific
properties -- replace with whatever your actual driver requires (or remove entirely
if your driver needs none beyond user/password).
Limitations of GENERIC mode:
- DDL generation uses generic SQL types, which may not match your database's actual
type system -- you may need to manually adjust types in the generated .jdx file.
- If generating CREATE TABLE statements, auto-increment columns won't have a
database-specific keyword appended automatically -- edit the generated .jdx.create
SQL script by hand to add the correct syntax for your database.
- Binary columns map to LONG VARBINARY by default -- override in the .jdx file if
your database needs something more specific.
Copy to your project root, rename to orm_skyway_config.json, and edit for your database.
Run: python orm_skyway.py -f orm_skyway_config.json --phase 1+3
